valueBasis: Per database reference portion: 100 g, 100 ml, or one item where applicable. BLS values are per 100 g. CoFID values are per 100 g except alcoholic beverages, which are per 100 ml. Values are converted only when a documented density or specific gravity is available.
nullPolicy: A source blank, dash, N, trace, or below-detection marker is not a numeric zero. It remains null until a reliable numeric value is found.

coverageNotes.BLS_4_0: BLS 4.0 provides total omega-3, total omega-6, and alcohol, but no total trans-fat component. Total trans fat remains null unless another source reports it; a single trans isomer is not used as a substitute.
coverageNotes.CoFID_2021: CoFID 2021 values are per 100 g except alcoholic beverages, which are per 100 ml. Tr and N remain nonnumeric markers.
coverageNotes.USDA_and_logical_zero_updates_2026_09_24: Added per-100-ml Omega values for maple syrup and apple juice using USDA SR Legacy household-portion gram weights and the US cup volume. The total-fat cross-check for both generic USDA matches differs from the database row and is recorded on the source records. Apple-juice trans fat remains null because exact CoFID reports Tr. Added family sums for Greek yogurt from specifically classified n-3/n-6 components while recording the 0.017 g/100 g unassigned PUFA residual. Added explicit composition-based zeros for dry/unfermented foods and selected non-oil plant foods; marker Tr and <LOD values were not converted to numeric zero.

components.FAPUN3: Total n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, g/100 g
components.FAPUN6: Total n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids, g/100 g

components.TOTn3PFOD: Total n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids per 100 g food
components.TOTn6PFOD: Total n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids per 100 g food
components.FODTRANS: Total trans fatty acids per 100 g food

DerivedTotalFatZero.citation: Derived from Total Fat (g) in the database, checked against numeric source values in the batch audit.
DerivedTotalFatZero.rule: For an exact database value of 0 g total fat, missing Omega-3, Omega-6, and trans-fat values may be derived as 0 g only when no positive numeric source value for that field contradicts the derivation.

USDA_FoodData_Central_SR_Legacy_2018.citation: USDA Agricultural Research Service, FoodData Central, SR Legacy, April 2018. Direct records and nutrient amounts per 100 g edible portion.
USDA_FoodData_Central_SR_Legacy_2018.omegaMethod: Sum reported n-3/n-6 components without double-counting undifferentiated totals; accept Omega-3/Omega-6 sums only when they reconcile to total polyunsaturated fatty acids within 0.01 g or 1 percent. Foods using ml or other units receive only source zeros until an approved conversion is available.

FDA_TransFat_Overview.citation: FDA, Trans Fat. Describes partially hydrogenated oils as the major artificial source and natural trans fat in ruminant foods; used only as context for composition-based zeros on non-oil plant foods.

records.note: Brand specification, not a universal average for every hemp oil.

records.sourceName: Sensory and phytochemical characteristics of poppy varieties, Table 1
records.method: mean fatty-acid percentages multiplied by mean oil density 0.91 g/ml
records.note: USDA poppyseed oil has numeric zero for alpha-linolenic acid, while the analytical variety study measured a mean of 0.50%; the study and BLS exact-food value (1.0 g/100 g) support a positive value. The USDA zero was treated as source-specific non-detection, not a universal absence.

records.sourceName: BLS 4.0 Bratöl/Frittieröl, pflanzlich; USDA soybean oil household measure density
records.method: BLS exact-food g/100 g values multiplied by 0.921432 g/ml (218 g per US cup / 236.588 ml)
records.note: A generic oil blend varies by formulation; values follow the exact BLS generic food entry and a standard vegetable-oil density.

records.sourceName: Oil, safflower, salad or cooking, high oleic (FDC 171027)
records.method: source trans-fat value per 100 g oil multiplied by 0.921432 g/ml
records.note: High-oleic safflower oil is an analogue for unspecified safflower oil; cultivar and refining affect trace trans fat.

records.method: zero inferred for non-hydrogenated cold-pressed seed oil; no animal fat or partial hydrogenation in the described product
records.note: The specification confirms cold pressing but does not separately print a trans-fat line; zero is process-based, not a label-declared value.

records.sourceName: Wheat germ oil fatty-acid review table, trans C18:2 n-6 value 0.71%
records.method: reported 0.71% trans linoleic acid multiplied by oil density 0.921432 g/ml
records.note: Estimate from a secondary review table; processing and refining can change trans levels.

records.sourceName: Poppy oil analytical profile across varieties, Table 1
records.method: zero inferred for the non-hydrogenated edible seed oil; measured profile reports cis fatty acids and no trans isomer
records.note: The study does not provide a separate total-trans assay; zero is a process/profile inference.

records.method: refined-cooking-oil analogue trans value per 100 g multiplied by 0.921432 g/ml
records.note: Generic frying-oil composition varies; this is a refined vegetable-oil estimate, not a direct measurement of the blend.

records.method: zero inferred for unhydrogenated cocoa butter; no ruminant fat or partial hydrogenation is specified
records.note: Source composition lists native cocoa-butter fatty acids but is not a total-trans measurement.

records.sourceName: Crude and refined shea butter fatty-acid composition study
records.method: zero inferred for non-hydrogenated shea butter; measured profile reports cis fatty acids and no trans isomer

records.method: zero inferred under the common full-hydrogenation route for coconut fat; full hydrogenation saturates double bonds and does not form trans isomers
